key_insight: GraphBEAT outperformed tested graph and sequence models for gastrointestinal cancer risk stratification while using substantially fewer computational resources.
clinical_relevance: The framework could support earlier identification of pancreatic, liver, and intestinal cancer risk from longitudinal health records; it is not a drug discovery method.
method: Groups diagnosis and laboratory events into time buckets to build patient-specific, temporally directed graphs.
Encodes event identity, observed value, and temporal position in graph nodes.
Combines context-aware, time-decay message passing with multi-head attention pooling.
evidence_signal: In multi-site EHR evaluations at 12-, 24-, and 36-month diagnostic lead times, GraphBEAT outperformed all tested baselines and required over 250× fewer operations per patient and over 20× fewer parameters than Transformer and LSTM models.
watch_item: The abstract does not report absolute predictive performance, calibration, or prospective clinical validation, leaving real-world utility uncertain.
paper_title: GraphBEAT: Graph-based Bucketized Event Aggregation Over Time for Early Risk Stratification of Gastrointestinal Cancers
